# Workflows

- `ci.yml` builds and tests on Linux and Windows for every pull request, and adds macOS on `main`, weekly and on demand. On Linux it first checks that every workflow action is pinned to a full commit SHA listed in `actions.allow`, then tests and runs the supply-chain check (`scripts/check-supply-chain.py`). Every platform restores in locked mode and fails if a lock file changes or appears; Linux then checks the dependency register (`scripts/dependency-register.py`). Every platform installs the graph surface's npm packages with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` on Node.js 24 with no shared cache, audits them, type-checks the surface and runs its tests. Projects outside the solution, such as the Visual Studio spike under `experiments/visual-studio/`, restore on every platform too, and Windows builds that spike into a VSIX with full MSBuild, found with `vswhere`. The rules are in `docs/dependencies/README.md`. Its `ci passed` job succeeds only when every build in the matrix succeeded; it and `secret scan` are the required checks.
- `secret-scan.yml` scans the full history with gitleaks, downloaded and verified against its published SHA-256, on every pull request and every push to `main`.

Workflows hold read-only permissions, never persist checkout credentials, use only GitHub-owned actions pinned to full SHAs, and opt out of .NET and test-platform telemetry.
